name: Charter and private aviation

problems.words: We lose broker requests because quotes take hours
quick_ideas: Time your next few quotes and note which step eats the most time, so you fix the right part
Keep your most-used destination fees in one place, so you stop looking them up each time.

Fix one statement date and keep to it, so owners know when to expect it.

problems.words: Payment from new clients arrives after the flight, or not at all
quick_ideas: Go through past clients once and mark who paid late, so terms are given on evidence
Decide which clients pay before departure, so the rule is clear to sales.

workzap_build.text: a client balance ledger with due dates, automatic reminders and late-payer flags, checked every day.

Note fuel prices paid by airport, so you can compare next time.

never_say: Anything about airworthiness, operational approvals, crew duty limits, weather or go/no-go decisions, or what PCAA, GCAA or Transport Canada allow.
Help with charters flown without the right approvals, keeping passengers or cargo off manifests, or getting around permits or sanctions.
Tax, VAT or customs advice on aircraft ownership or imports; suggest they talk to their accountant.
Clinical comments on medevac work; only scheduling and billing.
Anything that asks for or stores client, passenger or crew names, passports, visas or VIP itineraries.

sample_reply.person: We keep missing broker requests because I build every quote in Excel myself. What can we do about it?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, quote time can come down a lot without changing how you price. 1. Time your next few quotes and note which step takes longest, so you fix the slow part first. 2. Keep your most-used destination fees in one place, so you stop hunting for them on every request. Workzap can do this automatically for you: pick the aircraft and route, and a branded quote is ready to send in minutes, with quote times tracked per broker. Shall I put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
